title: How Do You Know If a Job Candidate Has the Passion for the Work
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note addresses a costly and demoralizing pattern: investing heavily in developing a new hire who turns out to lack real passion for the discipline and soon leaves for something else entirely. Since passion is nearly impossible to verify directly during recruiting, the piece proposes a single revealing interview question -- where do you see yourself in five to ten years -- arguing that most candidates answer with surprising honesty because they don't anticipate the question exposing a lack of commitment. The answer isn't presented as a hard filter but as a valuable data point alongside other signals.
points: Hiring people who lack real passion for the work is described as demoralizing and costly for teams.
A recommended interview question -- where do you see yourself in 5-10 years -- often reveals candid signals about commitment.
Candidates tend to answer this question honestly because they don't expect it to expose weak passion.
The answer is framed as one valuable data point, not a definitive litmus test on its own.
Repeated hiring misses on passion are said to damage team morale as new hires depart after major investment.
quotes: Nothing is more frustrating or deflating than investing months and years in training a new colleague for success, only to learn they lack the passion for the work and will seek an opportunity in another discipline elsewhere.

It’s nearly impossible during the recruiting process to discern whether a prospective team member has the passion, commitment, and interest to build their skills and engage in the work of the enterprise over the long term.
Asking prospective team members what they see themselves doing in 5-10 years will often reveal where their true passions lie.
Because prospective hires typically can’t see why an honest answer to the question would cause concern, they are commonly very open in their expression.
When it comes to passion for the work, the fewer misses the better.
